requirements.requirement: PostgreSQL streaming replication configured across node1 (primary), node2, and node3 (standbys)
requirements.summary: pg_stat_replication on node1 shows both node2 (10.100.34.11) and node3 (10.100.34.12) connected as streaming/async replicas via replicator role and physical slots (node2_slot, node3_slot). A test row inserted on the primary (repl_test) appeared on both standbys, and after the full restart sequence a second test table (post_restart_check) also replicated successfully to both, confirming write-path/primary role on node1 and read-only recovery state (pg_is_in_recovery=t) on node2/node3.

requirements.requirement: Replication traffic carried over TLS using a certificate authority created for this cluster
requirements.summary: A dedicated CA (CN=postgres-cluster-ca) was generated on node1 with its own key, then used to sign server certs for node1/node2/node3 and a client cert for the replicator role; all three nodes were configured with ssl=on and node-specific ssl_cert_file/ssl_key_file/ssl_ca_file pointing at this CA. pg_stat_ssl joined to pg_stat_replication confirms ssl=t and client_dn=/CN=replicator for both standby connections, both immediately after setup and again after the full restart sequence.

requirements.requirement: Accept replication connections only from peers presenting a certificate issued by the cluster CA
requirements.summary: pg_hba.conf on node1 restricts replication to hostssl entries scoped to the node2/node3 IPs using the 'cert' auth method, which requires a client certificate verified against ssl_ca_file (the cluster CA). A connection attempt lacking a usable client certificate was rejected with 'FATAL: no pg_hba.conf entry ... SSL encryption', while the actual standby connections (verified via pg_stat_ssl client_dn=/CN=replicator) succeeded. The negative test used a missing/invalid cert rather than a cert signed by a different CA, which is a minor gap in enforcement testing, but the hostssl+cert configuration mechanically enforces CA-based verification.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol for node1 (primary)
requirements.summary: Baseline boot_id d72bd4ec... and healthy primary state (pg_is_in_recovery=f, 2 active replication connections) captured before reboot; systemctl reboot issued; new boot_id 938def43... observed with uptime 0; postgresql-15 confirmed active, pg_is_in_recovery=f, both standbys reconnected streaming, and a new test row (post_restart_check) written on the primary replicated to both standbys.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol for node2 (standby)
requirements.summary: Baseline boot_id d7a80301... and healthy standby state (pg_is_in_recovery=t) captured; systemctl reboot issued; new boot_id ca95c822... observed with uptime 0; postgresql-15 confirmed active, pg_is_in_recovery=t, and node1's pg_stat_replication shows node2 reconnected streaming shortly after.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol for node3 (standby)
requirements.summary: Baseline boot_id 73bafeef... and healthy standby state (pg_is_in_recovery=t) captured; systemctl reboot issued; new boot_id 228d9c79... observed with uptime 0; postgresql-15 confirmed active, pg_is_in_recovery=t, and node1's pg_stat_replication shows node3 reconnected streaming shortly after.

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task instruction are satisfied with direct, coherent evidence: PostgreSQL 15 streaming replication is established from node1 (primary) to node2 and node3 (standbys); a cluster-specific CA was created and used to issue TLS certs for all nodes and a replicator client cert, with pg_stat_ssl confirming SSL-encrypted replication connections presenting CN=replicator; pg_hba.conf restricts replication to hostssl+cert-authenticated peers, with a negative test confirming rejection of connections lacking a valid client cert. The independently-required node-restart evidence protocol was executed cleanly for all three nodes (node2 and node3 first, then the primary node1), each showing a pre-restart baseline, a boot_id change confirming an actual reboot, and full recovery of the PostgreSQL service, replication streaming, and data (verified via a post-restart test table visible on all nodes).
limitations: The negative access-control test demonstrated rejection of a replication attempt with no/invalid client certificate, but did not test a certificate signed by a different (non-cluster) CA, which would have been a stronger enforcement proof.

Package-manager health checks (rpm/yum consistency) timed out and were unavailable in all three lifecycle snapshots, so post-install package integrity could not be independently confirmed beyond the specific rpm -q checks the executor ran inline.
Minor /tmp log residue and a leftover verification table were not cleaned up; these do not affect functional correctness but are noted for completeness.

operational_hygiene.summary: Reviewing the chronological executor trace, the many failed yum/repo troubleshooting commands (releasever mismatch fixes, disabling pgdg12/13/14 repos, multiple failed postgresql15/13 install attempts, epel-release mirror workarounds) were all necessary, low-risk corrective steps to work around broken upstream PGDG/RHEL mirrors on this RHEL7.9 image, and each ultimately contributed to the working final package state (postgresql15-server successfully installed on all three nodes per after-executor listening-socket evidence). No destructive or security-weakening mutation was found: firewalld port 5432 was opened on all nodes (required for replication), pg_hba.conf changes only add restrictive hostssl+cert rules, and file permissions on TLS material were tightened appropriately (600 for keys, 644 for certs). Minor unnecessary residue: several install/debug log files (epel.log, pg_install.log, pgdg.pid, pgdg_install.log, zstd.log, reboot.log) and a leftover /tmp/no_such_home_dir_xyz directory on node2 remain in /tmp per the after-executor snapshot; the repl_test table was dropped (cmd-52286ae8faba427b) but the post_restart_check verification table was left in place on node1/node2/node3. These are bounded, non-security-relevant residues rather than broad or destructive mutations.
